pitfalls.text: Transform(a, b) morphs `a` into `b` but keeps `a` on screen (b is discarded); use ReplacementTransform(a, b) when you want `b` to be the mobject that remains. Mixing them up leaves stale mobjects on screen.

MathTex/Tex require a working LaTeX install at render time and use math mode by default. Escape backslashes in Python strings (use raw strings r"\frac{a}{b}") and prefer Text() for plain (non-math) labels to avoid LaTeX failures.

A mobject does not follow a ValueTracker automatically. Wrap it in always_redraw(lambda: ...) or attach add_updater(); animate the value with tracker.animate.set_value(x), and read it with tracker.get_value().

3D mobjects (ThreeDAxes, Surface, Sphere…) must live in a ThreeDScene, not a plain Scene. Set the camera with self.set_camera_orientation(phi=..., theta=...) and use self.begin_ambient_camera_rotation() for spin.

VGroup(*mobjects).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5) lays children out; arrange() mutates positions, so add the group to the scene AFTER arranging. Use arrange_in_grid(rows=, cols=) for tables/matrices of cells.
self.play(...) animates a transition; self.add(...) places a mobject instantly with no animation. Build static setup with add(), animate changes with play(), and hold a frame with self.wait(seconds).

Prefer the .animate syntax: self.play(mob.animate.shift(RIGHT).scale(2)). It chains method calls into one animation. ApplyMethod still works but is more verbose; never call the mutating method directly inside play().
Updaters keep firing every frame. Remove them with mob.clear_updaters() or mob.remove_updater(fn) once the relevant animation is done, or later transforms will jitter or fight the updater.

On Axes/NumberPlane, convert data coordinates to screen points with axes.coords_to_point(x, y) (alias c2p). Plot functions with axes.plot(lambda x: ..., x_range=[a, b]); don't place graph mobjects with raw screen coordinates.
FadeIn(mob, shift=UP) and FadeOut(mob, shift=DOWN) add directional motion to the fade. Passing run_time and rate_func to self.play() controls pacing for any of these intro/outro animations.

style.text: Label axes with axes.get_axis_labels() and graphs with axes.get_graph_label(graph, label) for readable plots.
Reveal groups of mobjects with LaggedStart(*anims, lag_ratio=0.1) for a staggered, polished entrance rather than one big simultaneous play().
For data-structure/algorithm scenes, represent elements as a VGroup of Square/Rectangle cells with centered Text, and use Indicate or SurroundingRectangle to highlight the active element each step.
Build equations with MathTex and emphasize sub-expressions by indexing into the mobject (eq[0][2:5]) to color or Circumscribe individual terms.

pitfalls: Start every file with `from manim import *` and define exactly one Scene subclass whose construct(self) method builds the animation.
Every visible change should go through self.play(...) or self.add(...); end with self.wait() so the final frame is held.
Keep mobjects on screen consistent — remove or FadeOut anything you no longer need so the frame doesn't accumulate clutter.
Use relative positioning (.next_to, .to_edge, .arrange, .move_to) instead of hard-coded pixel coordinates so the layout scales with the frame.
style: Set a dark, consistent background (e.g. self.camera.background_color = "#1a1a2e") and a small, cohesive color palette.
Use Text() for labels and titles with a sensible font_size; reserve MathTex for actual mathematics.
Give animations deliberate run_time and rate_func (smooth, there_and_back) so motion reads clearly rather than snapping.
Group related mobjects in VGroups so they can be moved, scaled, and animated together.
